newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee claws back ground on arb, spec buying.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee claws back ground on arb, spec buying.

text.p: Robusta coffee futures recovered from an earlier bout of origin selling on Monday as arbitrage and speculative buyers moved into nearby positions late in the day's session, traders said.
But the key November contract's attempts to sustain a rally above resistance at $1,528 per tonne was shortlived and the position closed $13 higher at $1,527.
"There was some arb buying in London against New York," said one trader. "It (the London market) has been generally just holding its own rather than pushing ahead," he said.
Another market source said some short covering could have spilt into the market from the end of last week.
All positions ended firmer but off highs and overall volume reached 2,743 lots.
Sales from origins such as Ivory Coast and Indonesia pushed values lower amid a lack of buying, traders said.
U.S. certified stock figures are due out after the close of New York trading on Monday. Last week, news of a sharp drawdown to lowest levels for 12 years stirred prices higher.
Traders said a fresh draw could spark fund buying in New York but gains were likely to be capped with Central American supplies now on their way.
"It doesn't seem to want to break down at the moment so I think everyone is going to be content to see what happens after the close," said a trader.
